tagline: Europe's first independent orbital launcher — opened the commercial-comsat era for ESA, flew Giotto to Halley
dispatch: Ariane 1 was where Europe won its independence in space. Built after the United States made clear it would launch European satellites only on its own terms, Ariane 1 flew from Kourou in 1979 and gave Europe, for the first time, a launcher it fully controlled — answerable to no other power. It was a modest rocket by later standards, but the principle it established was not modest at all: that a continent's access to orbit should belong to that continent. Every Ariane since has flown that principle.
description: Three-stage rocket built by CNES at ESA's request after the cancelled Europa programme — hypergolic UH-25 / N2O4 first + second stages topped with the LH₂ / LOX HM7 third stage. 11 launches from Kourou between 1979-12-24 and 1986-02-22 carried 27 European telecom and science satellites including ECS-1, Marecs A/B, Spacenet, Telecom 1A/1B, and ESA's Giotto Halley flyby probe. Retired in favour of the bigger Ariane 2/3/4; the HM7 cryogenic upper-stage line lived on through Ariane 4 and into Ariane 5's ESC-A.
best_known_for: Europe's first independent orbital launcher — 11 flights 1979-1986, opened commercial comsats + Giotto to Halley
